newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks start 0.53 pct lower.
newsitem.headline: French stocks start 0.53 pct lower.

text.p: French shares opened 0.53 percent lower on Tuesday after a Wall Street slide and ahead of the Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Commitee (FOMC) this afternoon where no U.S. rate action is expected.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 11.11 points or 0.5 percent at 2,211.46 at 0905 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,214 from 2,227.5 on Monday's close.

Wall Street's drop was triggered by a late sell-off in technology stocks following some disappointing results and dealers said this was not symptomatic for the overall market but showed the market was fragile.
"There is really nothing going on, everbody is sitting on their hands," a dealer said. Volume was 430 million francs.

Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet will today outline the bank's monetary policy goals in an annual news conference. Economists said he is expected to steer clear of controversy when he sets the central bank's policy targets but may hint at more official interest rate cuts.

On Tuesday morning, Prime Minister Alain Juppe said he saw 1997 growth of at least 2.4 percent, a tick higher than Finance Minister Jean Arthuis who on Sunday said 1997 growth would be at least 2.3 percent.
After today's FOMC meeting and Bank of France news conference, investors will await the Bundesbank on Thursday.
French bond futures started much lower, while the franc and PIBOR remained a little weaker.

A rise in bunds was affecting French paper. German bonds rose in a recovery from Sunday's European stability pact and on the back of the Bundesbank's 1996 report, saying the bank's main monetary policy indicator -- M3 -- may overshoot by 4.0 to 7.0 percent at end 1996 and that German growth does not pose a danger to price stability. Technical analysts say the share market's recent recovery remained fragile.
